messages:
sara_sales: ACME POC — they want a Private deployment behind their transit VPC, preserve client source IP to our backend for audit, and allow TLS-inspect in their DMZ. Also asked for a cost comparison: dedicated EIP per AZ vs NAT gateway. Need checklist + short answer for customer.

eli_se: TL;DR: Private deploy + interface endpoints works. Preserving client src IP depends on topology: if traffic is hairpinned through a NAT Gateway you'll lose it. We can preserve with BYOIP/EIP or PROXY protocol.

mike_netops: Quick clarifying q: how are they terminating connectivity? Options impact NAT behavior: 1) PrivateLink (interface endpoints), 2) TGW peering/spoke model, or 3) site-to-site VPN into transit. Which one are they targeting?

sara_sales: They prefer Transit TGW for low-latency data paths between on-prem and cloud, but they like PrivateLink for control plane. Security wants explicit allowlist for firewall and a note on TLS-inspect (are we ok w/ proxy doing TLS-terminate?).

tanvi_sec: Security take: TLS inspect in DMZ is acceptable if customer retains cert ownership and we terminate mTLS on our connector. We will not MITM customer certs. For Private deploy we can support mTLS and customer-managed KMS for keying/audit. Will prepare wording for the security questionnaire.

eli_se: Sample allowlist / SG snippet for them to paste into firewall/security docs:

```
# Suggestion: customer outbound rules (egress to Redwood endpoints)
# Allow FQDN/URL-based if their firewall supports it; otherwise IP ranges we publish.
Outbound: TCP 443 -> redwood-private-endpoint.<region>.internal (FQDN) or published IPs
Outbound: UDP 123 -> 0.0.0.0/0 (NTP)
Outbound: TCP 443 -> redwood-healthcheck-ips (optional, for probes)

# Inbound only for healthchecks if they require
Inbound: TCP 443 <- redwood-healthcheck-ips (optional)
```

Also: we publish region IP ranges and FQDNs in onboarding doc. Recommend FQDN allowlist for sticky maintenance.

mike_netops: Preserving source IP options (practical):
- PrivateLink + NLB with static EIP on our side -> stable source and simplest for audit.
- Transparent proxy in customer's DMZ forwarding via PROXY protocol -> preserves original client IP to backend if app supports it.
- 1:1 SNAT (EIP per host) -> expensive but preserves source across NAT.
If they hairpin through a centralized NAT gateway (common TGW pattern) you will see TGW/NAT IP instead of client src.

sara_sales: Customer pricing question: "how much extra for dedicated EIP per AZ vs a NAT gateway approach?" Can we give a quick estimate?

eli_se: Pricing guidance: Dedicated static egress (per-EIP sticky mapping) is offered as a Private-deploy add-on — typically billed as a monthly per-EIP fee + usage egress. NAT-style (shared egress) is lower infra cost but we cannot guarantee stable per-customer source IP on failover. I'll capture exact $ amounts with finance and update — flagging billing.

deploy-bot: [deploy-bot] Onboarding checklist updated: https://redwood.internal/onboard/acme-poc/connectivity (link)

tanvi_sec: Security questionnaire items I'm adding: supported TLS versions (min TLS1.2), supported ciphers (example: TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256), mTLS support, PKI integration notes, audit log retention options, and KMS/HSM integrations for Private deploy. Will attach template answer.

mike_netops: Ops/triage notes: watch MTU when tunnels + encapsulation present (IPSec/GRE). Recommend conservative path MTU ~1400 to avoid fragmentation for streaming workloads. Also call out TCP keepalive (60s) and idle timeouts for long streaming connections.

eli_se: Action items (owners):
- Eli: produce one-pager comparison (PrivateLink vs TGW vs Peering) + diagram — include src-IP preservation tradeoffs and PROXY header example.
- Mike: draft DMZ proxy + PROXY protocol snippet and MTU guidance.
- Tanvi: draft security questionnaire answers (mTLS/ciphers/KMS/logging).
- Sara: gather pricing expectation from ACME and loop in finance for EIP vs NAT delta.

sara_sales: I'll sync with ACME tomorrow; they specifically asked for a one-page doc and a short checklist they can hand to NetOps.

mike_netops: One more operational callout: multi-region HA requires multi-region endpoints; sticky egress with failover across regions is harder — highlight as POC risk.

eli_se: I'll have the decision matrix and diagram by EOD. Will include sample SG, sample PROXY header example and quick pricing note (estimates) for ACME to review.

sara_sales: :thumbsup: Thanks team — please drop artifacts in the onboarding doc link and I'll share with the customer after the sync.
